work_order.understanding:
Two different things went wrong before this one, and both have to be named.

The first: the plan that built PR #9 diagnosed the ORIGINAL bug correctly and its fix works - QA passed AC-1 through AC-10 on a live browser, including the Group split, the table view and Type=Budgeted. What that plan never stated is the assumption it was quietly making, which is that the category conditions fully describe which categories can appear on the row axis. That assumption is false the moment the operator is 'any of', and its being false is BUG-1.

The second: my previous revision of this work order got that diagnosis right and proposed the right shape of fix, and was refused by the plan reviewer for one thing - AC-11, and the same assertion in tests[]'s e2e money case and in qa_script step 4, required the 'any of' TOTAL SPENDING to be at least as large in magnitude as max(notes-only, all-of), and the reviewer read the plan's own evidence as showing that a CORRECT fix would fail it (-7,900.41 against a notes-only branch of -8,302.84). I accept the substance of that objection. An acceptance criterion is re-checked by QA on every future run with no memory of this one, so it has to be a property the fix GUARANTEES; an arithmetic relation read off one run of one generated dataset is not that, whatever its true value today. AC-11, the e2e money assertion and qa_script step 4 are rewritten below on the relation the fix does guarantee - the row set - paired with a discriminator that is a statement about equality rather than about size.

I do not accept the reviewer's numeric premise, and the reason matters for how the new criteria are written. Its two figures are not two readings of one dataset. QA's runner (.sdlc/qa/playwright.config.mjs) uses devices['Desktop Chrome'] and never sets userAgent: 'playwright' - the repo's own e2e config does, at packages/desktop-client/playwright.config.ts:17 - so Platform.isPlaywright is false in a QA run (packages/loot-core/src/shared/platform.ts:10-13) and createTestBudget draws from Math.random (packages/loot-core/src/mocks/random.ts:16). The differential control was a worktree at /tmp/base served on a second port: a second origin, with its own demo budget, generated from a different Math.random draw. -7,900.41 and -8,302.84 therefore describe different data and cannot be compared. The same fact cuts the other way and is why this revision goes further than the reviewer asked: in a QA run the demo budget is NOT stable, so no absolute figure may be written into any criterion as an expected literal. What IS stable is the category NAMES, which are hard-coded (packages/loot-core/src/mocks/budget.ts:804-834) - which is why AC-11 can name 'Food' and must not name a number.

I reproduced the defect myself rather than taking QA's word for it. Extracting the PR's own narrowCategoriesByConditions and filterCategoriesByConditions from origin/sdlc/issue-4 and running them over a four-category fixture: with conditions [notes contains 'e', category oneOf ['c-cell']] the helper returns list ['c-cell'] and grouped [['g-bills',['c-cell']]] under 'or' - byte-identical to what it returns for the same two conditions under 'and'. That is the whole bug in one line: the axis is computed as though the category condition were the only condition, while the query side unions every disjunct. Add the gate proposed below and exactly two of the eight shapes I exercised change; 'or' with two category conditions, 'or' with a category plus a category_group, 'and' with notes plus a category, 'and' with a category alone, no conditions, and 'or' with a customName plus a category are all byte-identical, and the identity return AC-10 depends on survives.

Everything else from the previous revision is kept unchanged: the one-file fix, the decision to leave filterCategoriesByConditions byte-identical, the decision not to touch the query side, and AC-1 through AC-10 exactly as QA last saw and passed them.
work_order.root_cause: The PR's new helper narrowCategoriesByConditions (packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/budgetDataQuery.ts) forwards conditionsOp straight into filterCategoriesByConditions, which considers ONLY conditions whose field is 'category' or 'category_group' (budgetDataQuery.ts:85-94) and evaluates them with `.some` when conditionsOp is 'or' (budgetDataQuery.ts:171-177). Every other condition in the list is discarded without a trace. Under 'and' that is correct - a returned transaction must satisfy every condition, so a category condition genuinely filters the axis on its own. Under 'or' it is not: a returned transaction only has to satisfy ONE condition, so the category condition is a single disjunct among several and no longer describes the result set, and the helper narrows as if it did. The query side is not narrowed that way and never was: custom-spreadsheet.ts:115-118 sends the whole condition list to 'make-filters-from-conditions' and wraps the result in `{ [conditionsOpKey]: filters }` with conditionsOpKey '$or', which makeQuery.ts:28-30 turns into a genuine $or, so every disjunct's transactions are fetched. The axis and the query then describe different sets: transactions in categories the axis has just deleted are fetched, recalculate finds no row to attach them to, and their amounts are dropped from every total - silently, with no error, no empty state and no warning. 'Show empty rows' is not involved; the rows are gone from the axis either way. Measured by QA on one demo budget: notes-only -8,302.84, all-of -4,575.00, any-of -4,575.00 - the union collapsed exactly onto the 'all of' figure, and the row axis collapsed to Bills/Cell/Internet/Mortgage/Water/Power while the notes-only run immediately before it had rendered Food. I confirmed the same asymmetry at the function level: under 'or' the helper returns byte-identical output to 'and' for the same condition list. This is a defect INTRODUCED by this PR - before it the axis was unnarrowed under every condition set, which is a superset and therefore never loses money - and it went unnoticed because none of the PR's seven unit tests combines conditionsOp 'or' with a non-category condition.
work_order.approach:
Keep the previous plan's structure, which QA verified, and repair the one unsound step in it. Add a small predicate canNarrowAxisByConditions(conditions, conditionsOp) beside narrowCategoriesByConditions in budgetDataQuery.ts and call it as the first thing that helper does, returning `categories` unchanged when it is false and before it ever calls filterCategoriesByConditions. The predicate: false when there are no conditions; TRUE unconditionally when conditionsOp !== 'or', because a conjunctive result satisfies every condition, so a category condition does describe the axis by itself and the 'and' behaviour QA validated is untouched; and under 'or' TRUE only when every effective (non-customName) condition has field 'category' or 'category_group', because then the union of the disjuncts is itself a statement about the category axis and the existing `.some` evaluation is exactly right. Under 'or' with any disjunct on another field - notes, date, payee, account, amount - return false. The unnarrowed axis is main's behaviour and it is the safe direction: conditionsToAQL unions every disjunct on the query side, so an unnarrowed axis is a superset of the true result set, which costs empty rows under 'Show empty rows' and never costs money. Dropping money silently is the one failure mode that is not acceptable here.

Put the gate inside narrowCategoriesByConditions and NOT inside filterCategoriesByConditions. The latter has two callers this PR did not introduce - spending-spreadsheet.ts:60 and fetchBudgetData at budgetDataQuery.ts:203 - both untouched main code, and moving the gate there would change behaviour on both, widening the fix well past the defect. narrowCategoriesByConditions is the function this PR added and the only one it is responsible for; scoping the gate there leaves filterCategoriesByConditions byte-identical, which is what makes AC-7's Budgeted path and AC-8's existing suites provably unaffected rather than merely asserted.

Neither call site needs an edit: custom-spreadsheet.ts:91-97 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:43-49 already pass `conditionsOp === 'or' ? 'or' : 'and'` into the helper, which is exactly what the gate reads. Keep the identity-return guard the previous plan added, keep passing the unfiltered categories.list / categories.grouped to fetchSpreadsheetQueryData in both factories - the query side must stay untouched, because the fix is about the axis agreeing with the query, not about changing what the query asks for - and keep filterEmptyRows unchanged, since it was only ever what exposed the original defect and is correct for its job.

Do NOT try to widen the axis to the union of all disjuncts. A non-category condition is a predicate over a transaction, not over a category, so there is nothing to union it with at the axis level without running the query first; see alternatives_considered.

files.change: Add an exported `canNarrowAxisByConditions(conditions, conditionsOp): boolean` predicate immediately above `narrowCategoriesByConditions`, and make `narrowCategoriesByConditions` return its `categories` argument unchanged when the predicate is false, before it calls `filterCategoriesByConditions`. Predicate body: `if (!conditions || conditions.length === 0) return false;` then `if (conditionsOp !== 'or') return true;` then, disjunctive case only, `const effective = conditions.filter(cond => !cond.customName); return effective.length > 0 && effective.every(cond => cond.field === 'category' || cond.field === 'category_group');`. Comment each branch with why it is sound - conjunctive results satisfy every condition so a category condition filters the axis alone; disjunctive results satisfy only one, so a category condition is one disjunct and describes the axis only when every disjunct is itself about the axis. The `customName` exclusion is not optional: custom-spreadsheet.ts:116 filters those conditions out before building the query, so they are not disjuncts of the result set either. Leave `filterCategoriesByConditions` byte-identical and leave both call sites alone - custom-spreadsheet.ts:91-97 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:43-49 already pass `conditionsOp === 'or' ? 'or' : 'and'`, which is what the gate reads. I ran the PR's own two functions over eight condition shapes against this exact predicate: it changes only 'or' + [notes, category] and 'or' + [date, category], and leaves 'or' + [category, category], 'or' + [category, category_group], 'and' + [notes, category], 'and' + [category], no conditions, and 'or' + [customName, category] byte-identical; the `list === categories.list` identity return that AC-10 depends on still fires for the empty and uninterpretable cases.

review.title: Under conditionsOp 'or' with a non-category condition, narrowing the axis by the category condition alone silently drops fetched transactions from the report AND from its totals. The query side ORs every condition; the axis side ORs only the category ones.
review.detail:
Under conditionsOp 'or' with a non-category condition, narrowing the axis by the category condition alone silently drops fetched transactions from the report AND from its totals. The query side ORs every condition; the axis side ORs only the category ones.

`packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/budgetDataQuery.ts:86`

Evidence: Two conditions reachable together in the UI: the sidebar produces `{field:'category', op:'oneOf', value:[A]}` (CustomReport.tsx:232 setSelectedCategories) and the topbar FilterButton adds e.g. `{field:'payee', op:'is', value:'X'}` (ReportTopbar.tsx:234). ConditionsOpMenu.tsx renders the all/any FieldSelect whenever `conditions.length > 1`, so conditionsOp='or' is user-selectable. With conditionsOp='or': (1) custom-spreadsheet.ts:120 sets conditionsOpKey='$or' and makeQuery.ts:20 filters `{ $or: filters }` over the AQL built from BOTH conditions by `make-filters-from-conditions`, so a transaction in unselected category B paid to payee X IS fetched; (2) narrowCategoriesByConditions -> filterCategoriesByConditions builds `categoryConditions` from `conditions.filter(cond => !cond.customName && (field==='category'||field==='category_group'))` (budgetDataQuery.ts:86-98) - the payee condition is not in that list - then applies `op === 'or' ? categoryConditions.some(...) : every(...)` (budgetDataQuery.ts:173-177), so B fails the single category condition and is dropped from both `list` and `grouped`; (3) totalAssets/totalDebts/netAssets/totalTotals in custom-spreadsheet.ts:180-250 are accumulated by iterating `groupByList`, which no longer contains B, so B's fetched amounts are excluded from the totals too. Pre-fix B was on the axis and its amounts were counted, so the fix changes a report total. No test exercises conditionsOp='or' - all seven cases in custom-spreadsheet.test.ts use baseProps' 'and'.

Fix: Only narrow the axis when the category conditions are the whole story: bail out to the identity return when conditionsOp === 'or' and `conditions.length !== categoryConditions.length` (i.e. a non-category condition participates in the OR). Add a unit case with conditionsOp='or' and a second, non-category condition asserting the axis is left unfiltered.

review.title: The new e2e test is not executed by any check the pipeline runs, so its central assertion - an exact, order-dependent applied-filter string - is unverified. A wrong string ships green.
review.detail:
The new e2e test is not executed by any check the pipeline runs, so its central assertion - an exact, order-dependent applied-filter string - is unverified. A wrong string ships green.

`.sdlc/config.yml:168`

Evidence: .sdlc/config.yml has `e2e: ""` under verify, and .github/workflows/ci-verify.yml:251-252 reads that value and exits 0 with 'verify.e2e not configured - skipping'. So the ci-verify run on this PR (run 36975106769, job 'verify', conclusion success) ran typecheck/lint/unit and no Playwright. The new test at packages/desktop-client/e2e/reports.test.ts:210 asserts `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'category one of [Cell, Internet, Mortgage, 2 more items...]' })` is visible; that string is derived from the demo budget's category ordering rather than from anything the test controls. Tracing it: mocks/budget.ts:816-822 creates the Bills group as [Power, Water, Mortgage, Internet, Cell], but createCategory (budget/app.ts:309-327) calls db.insertCategory with no `atEnd`, which inserts at the head of the group (db/index.ts:465-486, shoveSortOrders with targetId = first existing id), and getCategoriesGrouped orders by `c.sort_order, c.id` (db/index.ts:346).
